summary: Validated the pending-order reconciliation fix end-to-end. Wrote 9 pytest cases covering all 8 scenarios in the review request (read-only check on real RUNECHA order, late-entry core bug, partial consumption, order-after-slip must-not-consume, normal FIFO + idempotent reconcile, slip reassignment A->B, reverse reassignment restoring A, delete-slip restores order). All 9 tests PASSED against the live preview backend. UI spot-check as qa_tester confirmed order #f0304185 (RUNECHA AUTOMOBILES, 9/29/2026) now shows status 'Dispatched · 10/2/2026 · Slip #938 — Fully dispatched'. POST /api/orders/reconcile?dry_run=true returned count=0 (idempotent, no further drift). All QA TEST customers/orders/dispatches created during tests were cleaned up (verified 0 remaining).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~9555 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into routers (orders.py, dispatch.py, customers.py, reconcile.py, auth.py) in a future refactor; not blocking for this fix.

_reconcile_customer_orders uses day-level string comparison (slip day >= order day). This is correct for the business case but assumes dispatched_at and order_date are stored as ISO strings with sortable YYYY-MM-DD prefixes; keep this invariant documented.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reconcile logic is validated end-to-end. The regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_reconcile_orders.py can be re-run safely (self-cleans). The sibling RUNECHA order #159cdf3d dated 9/30/2026 is intentionally still Pending (slip #948 dated 10/3 arrived BEFORE this order was entered on 10/4 — UI correctly surfaces a 'Possible timing discrepancy' card with Clear/Update/Delete actions); that is user-driven resolution, not a reconciliation bug.
rca of the issue: Pre-fix behaviour: Pending orders were only decremented at slip-punch time via FIFO on same-day/future slips. If an order was entered AFTER its slip was already punched (back-dated order_date, as the user does when transcribing paper orders), or a slip was reassigned to a different party, or an edit/restore pathway credited the wrong order, nothing walked back and matched the orphan slip qty to the Pending order. Fix: _reconcile_customer_orders() in /app/backend/server.py (~L5650) now re-walks each customer's pending orders oldest-first and, for every slip dated on/after the order date with matching item_ids and unattributed quantity (quantity minus known order_alloc or heuristic prior-dispatch coverage), applies the free qty to the pending order and persists an explicit dispatch.order_alloc[order_id][item_id]=qty so the attribution is frozen and future runs are idempotent. Hooks were added after POST /api/orders, PATCH /api/orders/{id}, POST /api/dispatch/off-order, PATCH /api/dispatches/{id}, plus admin POST /api/orders/reconcile. Verification: real RUNECHA order f0304185 is Dispatched with items=[]; reconcile dry_run reports count=0 (idempotent).
